# imGram Bot API

imGram is an independent chat service with a Telegram-style Bot API subset. imGram bot tokens are not Telegram tokens and must never be sent to api.telegram.org.

Canonical API root: https://bot.premsir.com
Method URL: https://bot.premsir.com/bot<TOKEN>/<METHOD>

Start here: https://github.com/kidrauhl123/imgram-bot-api/blob/main/CONNECT.md
Adapter UX contract: https://github.com/kidrauhl123/imgram-bot-api/blob/main/ADAPTER_GUIDE.md
API reference: https://github.com/kidrauhl123/imgram-bot-api/blob/main/BOT_API.md
Compatibility: https://github.com/kidrauhl123/imgram-bot-api/blob/main/COMPATIBILITY.md
OpenAPI: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kidrauhl123/imgram-bot-api/main/openapi.json

Supported methods:
getMe, sendMessage, sendPhoto, sendDocument, sendChatAction, setMessageReaction, sendChecklist, editMessageText, deleteMessage,
pinChatMessage, unpinChatMessage, toggleChecklist, appendChecklist,
getFile, setMyCommands, getMyCommands, deleteMyCommands,
getUpdates, setWebhook, deleteWebhook, getWebhookInfo.

sendMessage and editMessageText support parse_mode=HTML, MarkdownV2, or Markdown, and explicit Telegram-style entities. Without parse_mode/entities, a conservative Agent CommonMark subset is auto-detected. Bare @usernames are recognized automatically. Incoming Message objects include entities.

sendPhoto and sendDocument accept Telegram-style multipart uploads up to 50 MiB. sendChatAction supports typing and Telegram upload/record action names.

Incoming photo/document file_id values are downloadable: call getFile, then GET https://bot.premsir.com/file/bot<TOKEN>/<file_path>, and pass the bytes to the Agent's actual attachment or multimodal input.

Register stable bot commands with setMyCommands. imGram renders them in the chat command-menu button and when the user types `/`; default scope is supported.

When implementing an imGram adapter, put deterministic UX behavior in adapter code, not the model prompt: refresh typing every 4 seconds, coalesce streamed deltas into one message with editMessageText (recommended 800 ms edit interval), force a formatted final edit, and always stop typing/clean temporary reactions in a finally block. Expose pin_message as a real tool calling pinChatMessage; never claim success without an API response containing ok=true and result=true. Keep token and API root configurable; only the behavior policy is fixed.
Bot-authored editMessageText streaming updates hide the visible edited marker automatically; human message edits still show it.

Only documented methods and fields are supported. Prefer raw HTTP for v1. OpenClaw is experimental; stock CC Connect, Hermes, and nanobot integrations require adapters. For nanobot, configure both the Bot API base URL and file base URL as described in integrations/nanobot.md.
